key_reasoning.reason: Toggle spans the MCP subsystem (MCPServerDetails model in assistant.py, access_control.py allow-list, client.py wire gating, toolkit_service.py precedence resolution) and the Provider/DSP subsystem (ProviderBase/CreateProviderRequest/UpdateProviderRequest in provider.py, provider_service.py update() bugfix, provider_tool_factory.py invocation gating) plus an Alembic migration — 8 components across 2 subsystems and 3 layers, following an established boolean-toggle pattern rather than introducing new abstractions.

Extends the existing, established user_context-forwarding pattern from EPMCDME-13260 with an explicit opt-in gate defaulting to False (client.py drops user_context unless allow_user_context is set; provider_tool_factory.py only attaches user_context when provider_config.allow_user_context). Established pattern, but gates PII forwarded to external MCP servers and DSP providers, so bumped one level for the security/privacy-sensitivity red flag.

15 files touched in this commit range (2446146d4..705ca5f5d): 13 modified plus 2 new (the 633929ee02fa Alembic migration and the new tests/codemie/service/mcp/test_toolkit_service_three_state.py), crossing the 11-15 XL threshold.

Touches REST API/models (assistant.py, provider.py), Service (mcp/client.py, mcp/toolkit_service.py, mcp/access_control.py, provider/provider_service.py, provider/provider_tool_factory.py), DB-Persistence (Alembic migration adding the allow_user_context column with server_default false), and External (gates the payload forwarded to MCP-Connect and DSP provider tool invocations) — a 3-4 layer profile including a persistence migration.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: gates forwarding of user PII/context (email, name, roles, etc.) to external MCP servers and DSP providers — security/privacy-sensitive data flow.
